title: American Indian students represent under 1% of enrollment in San Augustine County schools for 2024-25
text:
American Indian students represent under 1% of enrollment in San Augustine County schools for 2024-25
San Augustine County school districts enrolled three American Indian students for the 2024-25 school year, a 200% increase compared to the prior year, Texas Education Agency data indicated.
The total enrollment for San Augustine County school districts reached 974 students in 2024-25. American Indian students accounted for less than 1% of the overall enrollment, making them the second smallest ethnic group in these districts.
Of the two school districts in San Augustine County, Broaddus Independent School District recorded the largest number of American Indian students for 2024-25, enrolling two students.
Each district highlighted in the story has its main offices in cities within San Augustine County.
A 2026 WalletHub study ranked Texas among the least-educated states in the country, placing it 41st out of 50 for educational quality and student results.
Texas operates the country's second-largest K-12 public school system, educating approximately 5.5 million students with a student-to-teacher ratio near 15:1.
| District | % of American Indian Students | Number of American Indian Students | Total Enrollment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Broaddus ISD | 0.5 | 2 | 377 |
| San Augustine ISD | 0.2 | 1 | 597 |
Information for this article was sourced from the Texas Education Agency. Source data are available here.
